entries.title: LARES-2 Satellite Measures Terrestrial Frame-Dragging at 0.1% Precision
entries.authors: Ignazio Ciufolini, Antonio Paolozzi, Erricos C. Pavlis, et al.
entries.institution: Sapienza Università di Roma, University of Texas at Austin, GFZ Potsdam, et al.
entries.summary: LARES-2 satellite, combined with LAGEOS and GRACE data, measures frame-dragging (Lense-Thirring effect) with relative uncertainty at one-part-in-a-thousand — an order-of-magnitude improvement. Places stringent constraints on Chern-Simons gravity and other alternative gravitational models.
key_findings: Frame-dragging measured to ~0.1% accuracy (previous best: ~2%)
303 COTS retroreflectors on nickel alloy sphere at ~5900 km altitude
Constrains scalar-tensor extensions including Chern-Simons gravity
Also improves Earth lunisolar tide determination
entries.c9_relevance: Directly validates general relativity in weak-field regime; constrains quantum gravity modifications. Connects to Cluster 2 (Quantum Gravity - LQC bounce models), Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - precision measurement), Cluster 5 (Topological Systems - gravitomagnetic field topology).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can validate gravitomagnetic effects in orbital mechanics simulations; compare with TNG halo spin data

entries.title: Entropic Time Emergence in Cold-Atom Mini-Universe
entries.summary: 24,000 ultracold rubidium atoms in isolated quantum system demonstrate 'entropic time' — time emerges from internal entropy redistribution without external clock. Bright/dark region oscillations resemble Big Bang/Big Crunch cycles. Schrödinger equation re-expressible using entropic time.
key_findings: Time emerges from system-internal entropy changes, not external clock
Arrow of time flows consistently from entropy gradient
Schrödinger equation valid under entropic time definition
Platform for testing quantum cosmology and black hole analogs
entries.c9_relevance: Foundational for quantum gravity time problem (Wheeler-DeWitt equation). Bridges Cluster 1 (Quantum Foundations - relational time), Cluster 2 (Quantum Gravity - cosmological models), Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - entropy as resource), Cluster 7 (Quantum Thermodynamics - entropic time).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can simulate entropic time in C9 SNN using free-energy minimization as 'internal clock'; test against physical manifold entropy tracking

entries.title: Synthetic Rotation Recreates Penrose-Zel'dovich Black Hole Energy Extraction in Lab
entries.authors: Hadiseh Nasari, Hady Moussa, Yoshiaki Kasahara, Arno Thielens, Andrea Alù
entries.summary: Stationary ring of electronic resonators with time-modulated properties creates 'synthetic rotation' exceeding light speed (pattern velocity, not physical). Electromagnetic waves extract energy and amplify — reproducing Penrose process and Zel'dovich superradiance without mechanical rotation.
key_findings: Synthetic rotation via programmed temporal modulation of resonator properties
Effective rotation speed can exceed c (no physical object moves >c)
Wave amplification matches Penrose-Zel'dovich predictions
Platform for extreme physics, wireless comms, photonics, quantum tech
entries.c9_relevance: Demonstrates Floquet engineering for extreme rotational physics. Connects Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - Floquet systems), Cluster 5 (Topological Systems - non-Hermitian wave dynamics), Cluster 6 (Neuromorphic Computing - temporal coding analogs).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can model synthetic rotation in C9 SNN using time-modulated connectivity; test energy extraction analogies in neural dynamics

entries.title: Real-Number Quantum Mechanics: Consistent Description Without Complex Numbers
entries.authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, Dagmar Bruß
entries.institution: Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, German Aerospace Center (DLR)
entries.summary: Replaces restrictive tensor product postulate with physically-motivated combination rule. Uses 'flag' bookkeeping to track imaginary components as separate real numbers. Reproduces all standard QM predictions including multiparticle entanglement that defeated 2021 real-number attempts.
key_findings: Complex numbers convenient but not fundamental to QM
New combination rule: action on one subsystem doesn't affect separate part
Flag system tracks phase information without imaginary unit i
Matches all experimental predictions of standard QM
entries.c9_relevance: Resolves foundational debate about mathematical structure of quantum theory. Impacts Cluster 1 (Quantum Foundations - QBism, Consistent Histories, Darwinism), Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - resource theories, entanglement as commodity).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can implement real-number QM simulator in C9; compare computational complexity with complex formulation

entries.title: Strong Coupling of Microwave Photon to Electron-on-Helium Qubit
entries.authors: Gerwin Koolstra, Elena O. Glen, Niyaz R. Beysengulov, et al.
entries.summary: First strong coupling between single electron motional state on superfluid helium and microwave photon in superconducting resonator. Coupling rate 118 MHz exceeds resonator linewidth and electron decoherence rate. Vacuum Rabi splitting confirmed. High-kinetic-inductance TiN resonator minimizes stray capacitance.
key_findings: Coupling rate 118 MHz — enters strong coupling regime
High-kinetic-inductance TiN superconductor boosts electric field at electron
Dephasing identified as dominant decoherence source
Path to spin-qubit readout and CMOS-scalable quantum computing
entries.c9_relevance: Novel qubit platform combining ultra-high coherence with CMOS scalability. Connects Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - new qubit modalities), Cluster 6 (Neuromorphic Computing - CMOS integration, hardware diversity).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can model electron-on-helium qubit dynamics in C9 quantum bridge; compare coherence times with superconducting/transmon baselines

entries.title: First Cyclic Superconducting Quantum Heat Engine
entries.authors: Tuomas Uusnäkki, Mikko Möttönen, et al.
entries.summary: Transmon qubit + resonator + quantum-circuit refrigerator implement Otto cycle at millikelvin temperatures. Single refrigerator serves as both hot and cold bath. Positive work output demonstrated. Autonomous operation could eliminate millions of microwave cables in future quantum computers.
key_findings: Otto cycle in superconducting circuit with positive work output
Quantum refrigerator provides both heating and cooling on demand
Autonomous heat engine could replace room-temperature readout electronics
Finland targets 1000 logical qubits by 2035; cable reduction critical
entries.c9_relevance: Quantum thermodynamics meets practical quantum computing. Bridges Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - qubit control), Cluster 6 (Neuromorphic Computing - autonomous systems), Cluster 7 (Quantum Thermodynamics - heat engines, resource theories).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can simulate quantum Otto cycle in C9 thermodynamic module; optimize for free-energy minimization analog

entries.title: Rethinking the Inductive Effect: Modern Computational Analysis Challenges Century-Old Textbook Concept
entries.authors: Mark C. Elliott, Edwin C. Johnson, Kasimir P. Gregory, Colan E. Hughes
entries.summary: Traditional inductive effect (electrons transmitted through bond chains) fails in modern computational analysis. Overall molecular electron distribution (molecular orbital approach) provides more accurate explanation. Not an overturning of organic chemistry but a teaching-model refinement.
key_findings: Inductive effect limited to immediately adjacent bonds in neutral molecules
Molecular polarizability/delocalized orbitals better explain long-range behavior
Simpler, more consistent framework for teaching and research
Implications for drug discovery, materials science, agrochemicals
entries.c9_relevance: Complexity science perspective on model refinement. Cluster 4 (Complexity Science - emergence, simplification at higher scales). Less directly connected to other clusters but represents paradigm evolution pattern.
entries.sandbox_notes: Computational chemistry simulation; less aligned with current C9 sandbox capabilities

entries.title: Relativistic Effects Break Down Textbook Triple Bond Structure in Heavy Elements
entries.authors: Deniz Kahraman, Jie Hui, Lai-Sheng Wang
entries.summary: Photoelectron spectroscopy of bismuth-carbon molecules shows triple bonds don't follow sigma+2pi structure. Spin-orbit coupling at relativistic speeds smears sigma/pi boundary. Structure resembles one pi + two hybrid sigma-pi bonds. Bismuth of interest for lead-free solar cells and quantum materials.
key_findings: Direct spectroscopic evidence of relativistic bond hybridization
Sigma-pi boundary 'smeared' in heavy elements
Bismuth as lead alternative in next-gen solar cells
Quantum materials and quantum computing applications
entries.c9_relevance: Relativistic quantum chemistry with topological implications. Cluster 1 (Quantum Foundations - Dirac equation regime), Cluster 5 (Topological Systems - spin-orbit coupling, heavy-element topology).
entries.sandbox_notes: Requires relativistic quantum chemistry simulation infrastructure

entries.title: JWST Confirms Earliest Supernova at z~7.3 (730 Million Years Post-Big Bang)
entries.authors: Andrew Levan, Nial Tanvir, et al.
entries.institution: Radboud University, University of Warwick, University of Leicester
entries.summary: GRB 250314A followed by JWST observation confirms core-collapse supernova at z~7.3. Light travel time: 13.1 billion years. Despite early universe conditions (higher mass stars, fewer heavy elements), supernova spectrum matches modern supernovae. Epoch of reionization context.
key_findings: Earliest directly observed supernova; previous record holder older
JWST infrared confirmation after 3.5-month wait for peak brightness
Time dilation factor 8.3x at z=7.3
Early universe supernovae appear identical to local ones
entries.c9_relevance: Cosmological evolution and structure formation. Cluster 2 (Quantum Gravity - early universe physics), Cluster 5 (Topological Systems - spacetime structure evolution).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can compare with TNG early universe halo data; test A_c evolution predictions against supernova rates

entries.title: Quantum Damping of Cosmological Shear: mLQC-I Bounce Model Resolves Anisotropy Problem
entries.authors: Wen-Cong Gan, Anzhong Wang, et al.
entries.institution: Baylor University, Jiangxi Normal University, State University of Rio de Janeiro, Universidade Federal Fluminense
entries.summary: Modified Loop Quantum Cosmology (mLQC-I) shows quantum geometric damping suppresses anisotropies during bounce. Highly anisotropic contracting universe emerges homogeneous/isotropic after quantum bounce without fine-tuning or exotic matter. Self-isotropization via non-perturbative quantum effects.
key_findings: Quantum bounce replaces Big Bang singularity
Anisotropies decay exponentially in deep quantum regime post-bounce
No exotic matter required — pure quantum geometry effect
CMB and primordial gravitational wave signatures predicted
entries.c9_relevance: Directly connects to your C9 bounce/loop quantum cosmology interests. Cluster 2 (Quantum Gravity - LQC, bounce models), Cluster 3 (Quantum Information - quantum geometry as information), Cluster 7 (Quantum Thermodynamics - entropy/arrow in bounce context).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can integrate with existing C9 LQC bounce simulations; test A_c phase transition predictions against isotropization mechanism

entries.title: Ephaptic Coupling: Electric Fields Guide Neural Activity Moment-to-Moment
entries.authors: Earl K. Miller, Dimitris Pinotsis, et al.
entries.institution: MIT Picower Institute, City St George's University of London
entries.summary: Local electric fields (mesoscale LFPs) actively organize neural spiking via ephaptic coupling. Granger causality shows field→neuron directionality dominates. Field strength proportional to LFP power variation. 'Neurons are citizens; electric fields are government.' Therapeutic potential for electric field manipulation.
key_findings: Electric fields exert top-down control on neural activity trial-by-trial
Ephaptic coupling strength ∝ LFP power variation
Cytoelectric coupling: fields alter neuronal cytoskeleton for synchrony
Therapeutic: field manipulation could rewire faulty circuits without targeting individual synapses
entries.c9_relevance: Directly relevant to neuromorphic computing and consciousness studies. Cluster 6 (Neuromorphic Computing - SNNs, field-based computation), Cluster 8 (Consciousness Studies - integrated information, field theories of consciousness).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can implement ephaptic coupling in C9 SNN architecture; test field-based synchronization against synaptic-only models

entries.title: Bacterial Memory Inheritance: E. coli Passes Environmental Knowledge to Descendants
entries.summary: E. coli stores environmental information and passes protein-based 'memories' to daughter/granddaughter cells. Mathematical model of bacterial learning resembles recurrent neural network. Growth-rate-driven memory closes modeling gap. Implications for antibiotic resistance and understanding memory origins.
key_findings: Bacteria make decisions based on past history, not just current environment
Protein expression changes inherited across generations
Mathematical model structurally similar to recurrent neural networks
Antibiotic resistance strategies must account for bacterial 'experience'
entries.c9_relevance: Complexity and consciousness foundations. Cluster 4 (Complexity Science - adaptive systems, active inference), Cluster 8 (Consciousness Studies - Cellular Basis of Consciousness theory, minimal cognition).
entries.sandbox_notes: Can model bacterial memory as RNN in C9; compare with sovereign manifold free-energy minimization
